LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 WRITING TO GIVE INFORMATION – DIALOGUE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue, part of Strand 6 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: What are the key features of a dialogue? 2. Why are values important when engaging in any business transaction?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. examine the features of a dialogue for effective writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create a dialogue on the theme for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the importance of dialogue writing in communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. examine the features of a dialogue for effective writing,

   Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. create a dialogue on the theme for information,

   Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. acknowledge the importance of dialogue writing in communication.

   Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaborate with peers to discuss the features of a dialogue,

2. role play a dialogue with peers on a topic related to the theme of indigenous trade,

3. sketch an outline of a simple dialogue on a topic related to the theme,

4. share their sketch with peers for review,

5. compose the dialogue based on the reviewed outline,

6. exchange their dialogues with peers and identify the main ideas in the dialogues,

7. organise their well written dialogues in the class portfolio. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaborate with peers to discuss the features of a dialogue,
2. role play a dialogue with peers on a topic related to the theme of indigenous trade,
3. sketch an outline of a simple dialogue on a topic related to the theme,
4. share their sketch with peers for review,
5. compose the dialogue based on the reviewed outline,
6. exchange their dialogues with peers and identify the main ideas in the dialogues,
7. organise their well written dialogues in the class portfolio. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: The learner shares ideas that inspire creativity when composing the dialogue based on the

reviewed outline.

• Communication and Collaboration: These are enhanced as the learner shares their sketch with peers for review.
